analysis:
Examined the standalone (local) server changes. StandaloneServer+StartupPreload.swift (head lines 42, 50-75) adds a shapeWarmup dependency to StartupPreloader, a startupShapeWarmup helper that calls bridge.runShapeWarmupBeforeServing() before the listener opens, and scheduleShapeWarmups / retryShapeWarmups. retryShapeWarmups is gated on lifecycleState == .running and !lifecycleDraining (head line 72). StandaloneServer.swift (lines 562-567) changes the kv sweep Task to capture self weakly and call retryShapeWarmups() on each tick. The sweep task is cancelled and awaited in finishShutdown (lines 662-687), and the weak capture avoids a retain cycle. The guard on lifecycle state prevents warmups from starting during stopping or draining.

Security relevance: this is availability and perf scheduling inside the local standalone path. It adds no new network surface, no changes to coordinator/provider crypto, attestation, authorization, or prefix-cache storage (T-041), and no new data persistence or logging of prompt content. Warmup uses internal shapes with no consumer data, as far as the patch shows. Warmups yield to requests per the comments; there is no evidence of a DoS regression (T-010/T-029 are not materially affected).

Unverified contracts: the implementations of EngineV2Bridge.startShapeWarmupIfNeeded and runShapeWarmupBeforeServing, and the StartupPreloader changes (shapeWarmup dependency), are outside the supplied evidence. The next pass should confirm that warmup uses synthetic inputs only (no consumer plaintext, no prefix-cache donation to SSD that would touch T-041 at-rest artifacts), that it is preempted by requests, and that it respects memory admission (the KV budget and the load gate) so it cannot overcommit memory. The onRetired callback re-entering scheduleShapeWarmups on the actor could race with shutdown, but retryShapeWarmups gates only the sweep path; scheduleShapeWarmups from onRetired is not gated by lifecycle state. This is a minor lifecycle question, not a demonstrated vulnerability.
